newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian papers praise freedom, blast politicians.
newsitem.headline: Indian papers praise freedom, blast politicians.

text.p: Indian media gave mixed grades to half-century of independence on Friday and said corruption had tainted the legacy of a decades-long movement for freedom from British colonial rule.
Newspaper editorials exhorted Indian people for another "tryst with destiny" to rid the nation of the growing malaise blamed on power-hungry politicians.

"The time has come for the people who have watched growing decadence from the sidelines to think of ways to ensure that during the next few years the country finds a sense of direction and some purpose," H.K.Dua said in a front-paged comment in the Times of India newspaper.
Editor Hari Jaisingh said in The Tribune: "As a nation, we must take a vow that during the next 50 years the freedom we practise must be people-friendly and not personal power-cum-greed oriented."
"Let us have another "tryst with destiny" revolving around an enlightened concept of freedom for citizens," he added.
India needs a pledge to unshackle its soul "from the bondage of poverty, ignorance, illiteracy, intolerance and everything else that is ignoble," Chandan Mitra said in the Pioneer.

"It is nothing but tragic that in a country's scam-ridden politics, the very source of power -- the people -- hardly matters. The people are used only as tools for the politicians vote bank once in five years or so," Jaisingh said.
"Their disregard for values and decency in public life is matched by greed and untamed ambition," Dua said.
"As the years have gone by, the dream (of building a new India) has turned into a nightmare; idealism has been replaced by cynicism," he said.
The Observer of Business and Politics termed slippages on the economic and social fronts as "pinpricks" compared to the decline of institutions of India's republic.

Jaisingh blamed a widely-seen nexus between politicians, bureaucrats and the underworld for growing corruption. "The nexus has to be broken if India has to regain a pride of place in the comity of nations," he said.
